EUR.catalyst: The euro holds near 1.1627 against the greenback, trading above its 20-day and 50-day moving averages while testing resistance at its 200-day moving average. The European Central Bank left its key deposit rate unchanged at 2.00% at its latest policy meeting, with President Christine Lagarde signaling a steady rate outlook as eurozone inflation and growth indicators beat expectations. Money markets widely expect the ECB to maintain current policy settings for the remainder of the year, backed by Nomura forecasts highlighting long-term ECB-Fed policy divergence. Institutional focus turns to upcoming Eurozone retail sales and inflation updates to gauge whether tightening risks could re-emerge in 2026.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen has surged across G10 crosses, delivering a G10-leading 1-week gain of +1.48% as market participants aggressively price in upcoming Bank of Japan rate hikes and potential FX intervention. Spot pricing has broken below technical support clusters toward 153.96 against the dollar, backed by 1-month 25-delta risk reversals showing extreme downside put skew at -2.46. Strong domestic fundamentals have bolstered the hawkish repricing, with the Reuters Tankan index highlighting factory sentiment at a near five-year high on robust semiconductor demand. The policy outlook hinges on the Bank of Japan's rate decision on September 18, where markets anticipate further policy normalization.

Strong household spending and construction data have further reinforced September rate hike bets, with traders looking to Chinese inflation data and Australian Consumer Inflation Expectations for near-term directional cues.
